# HTML-in-Canvas Demos

> Interactive demos and documentation for the WICG HTML-in-Canvas
> specification, which draws real, styled, accessible DOM elements
> into a `<canvas>` via `drawElementImage()`.

This site is a community resource maintained by En Dash Consulting with
demos of live HTML painted into a canvas: real text editing, native i18n, accessible chart labels, video
recording from HTML scenes, WebGL and WebGPU shader effects on DOM
content (including a demo built on Vercel's vgpu library), and 3D
scenes that use HTML elements as textures. The API is on by
default in Chrome 157 and later. Chromium 147–156 and Brave Stable have
it behind `chrome://flags/#canvas-draw-element` (`brave://flags/...` in
Brave).

## Spec primitives

- `<canvas layoutsubtree>` — opts the canvas's direct child elements
  into layout, hit testing, and accessibility while keeping their
  rendering invisible until explicitly drawn. Chrome 157+
  renamed this to `<canvas content="drawable">` and also requires a
  `drawable` attribute on each drawn child; set both spellings.
- `ctx.drawElementImage(element, x, y, ...)` — paints a `drawable`
  child of the canvas into the canvas. In Chrome 155+ it returns nothing
  and the browser keeps hit testing in line with the drawn position;
  earlier builds returned a `DOMMatrix` to apply as a CSS transform.
- `canvas.onpaint` / `canvas.requestPaint()` — paint event lifecycle
  for canvas children. The browser's paint pipeline runs and generates
  the cached paint records that `drawElementImage` depends on.
- `canvas.captureElementImage(element)` — produces a transferable
  `ElementImage` snapshot for use in `OffscreenCanvas` workers.
- WebGL equivalent: `gl.texElementSubImage2D(...)` into a texture you
  allocate first (`texElementImage2D` was removed in Chrome 157)
- WebGPU equivalent: `queue.drawElementImageToTexture(...)`
  (`copyElementImageToTexture` was removed in Chrome 157)

## Browser support

Chrome ships it on by default from 157. Other browsers have not
announced implementations yet.

- Chrome 157+: on by default
- Chromium 147–156: behind `chrome://flags/#canvas-draw-element`
- Brave Stable ≥ 1.89.132 (Chromium 147+), behind `brave://flags/#canvas-draw-element`
- Firefox: not implemented
- Safari/WebKit: not implemented

## Demos

Every demo lives at `/demos/{slug}/` (wrapped page with description,
metadata, and source viewer) and `/demos/{slug}/demo.html` (standalone
HTML file you can fork). The demo source is in
`src/content/demos/{slug}/demo.html` of the repository above.

- /demos/hello-world/ — minimal `drawElementImage` example: one DOM
  element painted many times in an animated ring with motion trails
- /demos/accessible-charts/ — bar + pie charts whose labels are real
  HTML with ARIA, focus rings via `drawFocusIfNeeded`
- /demos/interactive-form/ — sign-up form whose every input, select,
  slider, checkbox, and button is a real DOM element
- /demos/multi-element-composition/ — drag-and-drop cards with
  per-element transforms and z-order shuffling
- /demos/internationalized-text/ — `fillText()` vs `drawElementImage()`
  for RTL, vertical CJK, Thai, mixed-direction, emoji, and ruby
- /demos/rich-text-canvas-editor/ — contenteditable text inside a
  canvas with multi-pass canvas effects (glow, shadow, outline)
- /demos/html-to-image/ — replace `html2canvas` with one native API
  call: render a styled card and download as PNG/JPEG
- /demos/html-video-recording/ — `captureStream()` + MediaRecorder on a
  canvas painting live HTML, output as WebM
- /demos/offscreen-canvas-worker/ — `captureElementImage()` +
  `OffscreenCanvas` transfer to a Web Worker
- /demos/3d-room-live-content/ — Three.js scene with HTML elements
  used as textures on planes; first-person walkthrough
- /demos/css-to-shader/ — live CSS editor whose output is captured
  via `drawElementImage` and post-processed by a WebGL fragment shader
- /demos/frosted-glass-backdrop/ — multi-layer compositing with custom
  WebGL blur kernels (gaussian, directional, tilt-shift)
- /demos/liquid-glass/ — refraction distortion via WebGL applied to
  HTML content captured into the canvas
- /demos/elastic-bulge/ — mouse-driven elastic displacement: a WebGL2
  shader warps laid-out HTML content around the pointer
- /demos/vgpu-shader/ — WebGPU shading of live HTML using vgpu
  (https://github.com/vercel-labs/vgpu, Vercel's TypeScript WebGPU
  library): `drawElementImage` paints a real DOM card into the canvas,
  those pixels upload to a GPU texture, and a WGSL foil effect warps
  them on hover while hit testing stays on the underlying DOM. The
  still beside it is a `target.read()` of the same pass, standing in
  for rendering the identical shader headlessly through
  `vgpu/node` (Dawn) for OG images and CI snapshots
- /demos/pixel-disintegration/ — `getImageData()` on rendered HTML
  drives a particle scatter / reassemble effect
- /demos/morphing-text-transitions/ — pixel-level blends between two
  entirely different HTML layouts (crossfade, dissolve, wave, sort)
- /demos/page-curl-book-turn/ — cylindrical WebGL deformation that
  curls a captured HTML page like a turning book

## Project

- License: MIT
- Built with Astro 6, vanilla TypeScript, and Playwright
- Maintainer: En Dash Consulting (https://endash.us)
- Contributing: open a PR with a new folder under `src/content/demos/`
  containing `meta.json` + `demo.html`. The site picks it up
  automatically. See https://html-in-canvas.dev/contributing/ for the
  full guide.

## More from En Dash (the maintainers)

Free interactive courses that run in the browser, no API key:

- [Learn vgpu](https://endash.us/apps/learn-vgpu) — edit WGSL live and step the vgpu API (init, effect, frame, target), with the same program shown for browser, Node, and CI. The closest companion to the vgpu-shader demo above.
- [Learn LangGraph](https://endash.us/apps/learn-langgraph) — step a live graph: state, cycles, interrupts, multi-agent.
- [Learn LangChain](https://endash.us/apps/learn-langchain) — one job run four ways: chain, create_agent, Deep Agents, LangGraph.
- [Learn AgentCore](https://endash.us/apps/learn-agentcore) — the production half: sessions, identity, policy, memory.
